Treewidth is an important parameter in algorithmic and structural graph theory that measures how similar a graph is to a tree; see the survey [11].

Seymour [14] proved that the treewidth of a graph is bounded from above by a linear function of its separation number.



Theorem 2 ([14]).



For every graph GG, tw⁡(G)⩽4​sep⁡(G).\tw(G)\leqslant 4\sep(G).





Inspired by this, Abrishami et al. [1] conjectured that this characterisation of treewidth has a coarse analogue. We say that a graph GG admits (k,r)(k,r)-balanced separators if, for every vertex-weight function μ:V⁡(G)→ℝ⩾0\mu\colon V(G)\to\mathbb{R}_{\geqslant 0}, there is a (k,r)(k,r)-centred set which is a balanced separator for μ\mu.



Conjecture 3 ([1]).



For all k,r∈ℕk,r\in\mathbb{N}, there exist k′,r′∈ℕk^{\prime},r^{\prime}\in\mathbb{N} such that every graph that admits (k,r)(k,r)-balanced separators has a (k′,r′)(k^{\prime},r^{\prime})-centred tree decomposition.





The same argument that shows sep⁡(G)⩽tw⁡(G)+1\sep(G)\leqslant\tw(G)+1 also implies that every graph that has a (k,r)(k,r)-centred tree decomposition admits (k,r)(k,r)-balanced separators. Therefore, this conjecture, if true, would provide a balanced separator characterisation for coarse treewidth.




In this paper, we verify Conjecture 3 for hereditary Kt,tK_{t,t}-induced-subgraph-free graph classes in the r=1r=1 case.



Theorem 4.



For all k,t∈ℕk,t\in\mathbb{N}, there exists k′∈ℕk^{\prime}\in\mathbb{N} such that the following holds: Let GG be a Kt,tK_{t,t}-free graph such that every induced subgraph of GG admits (k,1)(k,1)-balanced separators. Then GG has a (k′,2)(k^{\prime},2)-centred tree-decomposition.





Together with Theorem 1, this gives a natural sufficient condition for a graph to be quasi-isometric to a graph with bounded treewidth.




Note that our proof for Theorem 4 gives the following stronger property: the radius-22 neighbourhoods can be taken with respect to the subgraph induced by the corresponding bag of the tree-decomposition.
